title: The AI Hype Index: AI is everywhere
gist: A short, satirical MIT Technology Review 'AI Hype Index' vignette arguing AI has become inescapable in daily life — from Google's AI Overviews (which the author says cost Google billions in lost ad revenue) to humanoid cleaning robots, AI-assisted cyberattacks and AI-saturated entertainment. Thin piece; the trailing 'Deep Dive' links are site navigation and were not extracted.

insights.claim: MIT Technology Review's AI Hype Index frames AI as spreading into every corner of daily life 'like a nasty rash', with the experience of the world now resembling 'a long, unskippable mobile ad'.
insights.speaker: Amit Katwala
insights.so_what: Signals rising consumer/cultural backlash against AI saturation; watch sentiment and engagement metrics for AI-forced product features.
insights.quote: Like a nasty rash, AI seems to spread everywhere.
insights.locator: Like a nasty rash, AI seems

insights.claim: Google pushes AI Overviews on users even though, per the author, the feature costs the company billions of dollars in lost ad revenue.
insights.speaker: Amit Katwala
insights.so_what: Search ad cannibalization from AI answers is a key Alphabet margin risk; track paid-click growth and search revenue per query.
insights.quote: Google crams AI Overviews down your throat even though it costs the company billions of dollars in lost ad revenue.
insights.locator: Like a nasty rash, AI seems

insights.claim: AI-powered humanoid robots are depicted as already being carried into apartments to clean rooms, suggesting consumer home-robotics deployments are becoming visible in everyday urban life.
insights.speaker: Amit Katwala
insights.so_what: Early anecdotal sign of home humanoid adoption; watch unit shipments and pricing from humanoid robot makers.
insights.locator: Like a nasty rash, AI seems

insights.claim: The author cites an AI-assisted cyberattack that caused supermarket ice cream to melt, illustrating that AI-enabled attacks are now reaching physical retail infrastructure such as refrigeration.
insights.speaker: Amit Katwala
insights.so_what: AI-assisted attacks on operational/IoT systems broaden the cybersecurity addressable market beyond IT.
insights.locator: Like a nasty rash, AI seems

insights.claim: AI figures have become mainstream cultural subjects: Sam Altman is portrayed by Andrew Garfield in a film, and Elon Musk has released a 'Grok-fied' version of The Odyssey.
insights.speaker: Amit Katwala
insights.so_what: AI-generated and AI-themed media is now mass-market; watch Grok/xAI moves into generated entertainment content.
